title: operational-value-map-for-managed-ai-decision-scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for AEs/SEs/marketing to map customer operational scenarios to Redwood differentiation vs cloud managed AI endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure). Not a polished executive brief — think: field-ready talking points, demo hooks, pricing & SLA framing, and common rebuttals.

Executive summary (one line):
Buyers pick managed endpoints when they want simplicity; they choose Redwood when they want predictable economics, operational controls, and resilience at scale.

Primary customer archetypes we target in these conversations: 
- Platform/AI infra teams at mid-market/enterprise who own latency/cost SLOs.
- Product/feature teams who need low-latency, predictable costs for chat/assistants.
- Regulated customers who require private deployments or deterministic isolation.

Operational decision scenarios (quick map):
1) Velocity-first (PoC to Prod in weeks)
- Hyperscaler angle: integrated with cloud tooling, single bill, managed models.
- Buyer need: quick dev time, minimal infra work.
- Redwood angle / win theme: Hosted API for fast ramp + clear migration path to Dedicated/Private without re-architecting code or losing telemetry. Emphasize same API surface and SDKs across modes.
- Demo hook: 10-min quickstart showing token-level cost dashboard and switching from hosted to dedicated in config without changing client code.

2) Cost-predictability / unit economics (scale beyond PoC)
- Hyperscaler angle: pay-as-you-go, some discounts but opaque per-token/unit variability.
- Buyer need: predictable monthly spend, visibility into per-route drivers.
- Redwood angle / win theme: Reserved capacity (Dedicated) + Optimize toolkit gives concrete batching/kv-cache suggestions that reduce token cost by X–Y% for common workloads. Call out transparent per-token math and tooling that simulates cost with config changes.
- Demo hook: cost-simulator: input throughput + avg length -> shows Dedicated commit recommendations and expected % savings vs hyperscaler managed endpoint.

3) Reliability & graceful degradation (SLOs across outages)
- Hyperscaler angle: global infra and multi-zone HA, but managed endpoints often black-box fallback behavior and cold-start variance.
- Buyer need: steady tail-latency, predictable fallbacks during region or model degradation.
- Redwood angle / win theme: Smart routing + model fallback policy (can route to cheaper variant or local replica) and mixing Dedicated and Hosted tiers to guarantee critical traffic. Emphasize automatic KV/prefix cache reuse to reduce cold-start variance.
- Demo hook: failover demo — simulate capacity spike in primary region and show automatic fallback to smaller-latency model and customer-configured QoS policy.

4) Data governance & isolation (sensitive/regulatory)
- Hyperscaler angle: VPC peering / private endpoints, but often limited observability and long procurement for enterprise contracts.
- Buyer need: customer-managed network, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, air-gapped options.
- Redwood angle / win theme: Private deployment option with customer-managed control plane, audit logs out-of-the-box, and on-prem package for air-gapped needs. Position as faster procurement path vs negotiating hyperscaler managed service add-ons.
- Demo hook: architecture diagram + compliance checklist that maps to SOC2/GDPR items.

5) Ops/Platform ownership & standardization
- Hyperscaler angle: one cloud for infra standardization; managed endpoint reduces infra overhead but can fragment stack across business units.
- Buyer need: consistent inference API across teams, reproducible rollouts, and centralized observability.
- Redwood angle / win theme: Unified API + Console (per-route dashboards, tracing, rollouts) so platform teams can enforce standards and observe regressions. Call out rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallbacks.
- Demo hook: show per-route alerting + token-level cost attributions and how a platform team sets guardrails for product teams.

Key differentiators to stress (words to use):
- Predictable economics, not just raw throughput
- Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private
- Ops-first controls (rollouts, tracing, per-route cost)
- Model fallback + routing policies for resilience
- Quantization and batching recommendations tied to actual workload profiles
- Transparent unit-cost simulation (saves time in procurement conversations)

Quick rebuttals / FAQ (field notes):
Q: Why not just use the cloud provider’s endpoint?
A: If you prioritize simplicity for tiny workloads, hyperscaler is fine. But once you need predictable bills, low tail-latency, or private deployment, the hidden costs and limited operational controls become friction points. We help customers avoid repeated re-architecture by providing the same API and migration path across deployment modes.

Q: Aren’t hyperscalers cheaper at scale?
A: They may be on gross GPU spend, but we win on unit economics because of smarter batching, prefix caching, and reserved capacity for predictable workloads. Show cost-simulator output vs a hypothetical hyperscaler-managed endpoint with assumptions.

Q: How do you handle model updates and regressions?
A: Rollouts in Console: canary A/B, automatic rollback on metric regressions tied to eval/prompt sets. Call out that hyperscaler endpoints rarely provide integrated regression alerting.

Q: What about data residency and compliance?
A: Private deployments and Dedicated with KMS/HSM integrations plus audit logs. We provide architecture and procurement templates to shorten security reviews.

Suggested play sequences for AE + SE calls (concise):
- Discovery (15 min): confirm scale, SLOs (p50/p95/p99), data residency, and cost predictability needs. Bring up existing pain with hyperscaler billing or cold start variance.
- Technical validation (30–60 min SE-led): demo latency profiles, cost simulator, and rollback/rollout flows.
- Procurement + pilot (internal): propose 3-month Dedicated pilot with commit sizing (use Optimize recommendations) and regular eval checkpoints on latency and quality metrics.

Competitive intelligence snippets (notes from field):
- AWS Bedrock: strong enterprise integrations and billing hooks; customers cite complexity and variable per-request cost. Some teams frustrated by limited fallbacks when models are throttled.
- GCP Vertex AI: great for ML teams already on GCP; strong MLOps integrations. Customers call out limited per-token cost visibility and hard-to-tune inference performance.
- Azure OpenAI / Managed endpoints: convenient for MS ecosystem; procurement and compliance with Azure AD is a plus. But embedding custom quantized models and private on-prem footprints is cumbersome.

Unresolved questions to validate with engineering/product:
- Can we quantify typical % saving for chat-heavy workloads when using Optimize + Dedicated vs hyperscaler managed endpoint? (ask applied-ml for two sample workloads)
- Precise SLA language we can promise for hybrid fallbacks (hosted + dedicated combos) — legal needs wording.

Collateral suggestions (marketing/ops):
- One-pager: "Predictable Inference Economics" with a small cost-simulator snapshot and 3 customer mini-case studies.
- Slide deck: 6 slides for AE: problem, hyperscaler gap, Redwood solution, demo flow, pilot offer, next steps.
- Battle-card: 1-page quick rebuttals + links to product docs and cost-sim tool.

Opening lines for pitches (copy options):
- "If your team cares about predictable bills and predictable latency, you shouldn’t have to pick between cost and availability — Redwood makes both possible."
- "We give platform teams the controls they need to standardize inference across orgs without reinventing rollout and billing logic."
- "Migration path: start on our hosted API, then move to Dedicated or Private without refactoring your clients."

Notes to marketing: keep language ops-forward and avoid purely 'model' claims. Buyers in these scenarios care about economics, observability, and operational resilience more than raw model accuracy.

Field checklist before pilot handoff:
- Confirm SLOs and peak QPS + token lengths
- Provide cost-simulator output and Dedicated commit recommendation
- Identify 3 eval prompts for regression monitoring
- Security packet (KMS, VPC diagram, audit log detail)

Slack quick-links to share in field threads:
- confluence://predictable-inference-economics (placeholder)
- jira://JIRA-GTM-421 (pilot template)

Working open items (for next revision):
- Add 2 anonymized cost-comparison examples (chat bot & reranker) from prod customers
- Better phrasing for hyperscaler strengths so AEs can use them as 'acknowledge' lines
- Capture specific legal language for Dedicated SLA + fallback policy

Author notes: this is intended to be used directly by AEs/SEs in calls and by product marketing as a source for a slim one-pager. Keep it short, keep it operational, and iterate after 3 field wins where we used this play.
